title.zh: 卷255 列傳四十二 张勇 赵良栋 王进宝 孙思克
title.en: Volume 255 Biographies 42: Zhang Yong, Zhao Liangdong, Wang Jinbao, Sun Sike
title.raw: 卷255 列傳四十二 张勇 赵良栋 王进宝 孙思克

sentences.zh: 列傳四十二

translations.literal: Biographies 42
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 42

sentences.zh: 張勇趙良棟王進寶王萬祥孫思克馬進良

translations.literal: Zhang Yong, Zhao Liangdong, Wang Jinbao, Wang Wanxiang, Sun Sike, Ma Jinliang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong, Zhao Liangdong, Wang Jinbao, Wang Wanxiang, Sun Sike, and Ma Jinliang

sentences.zh: 張勇，字非熊，陝西咸寧人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong, style name Feixiong, was a native of Xianning in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong, whose style name was Feixiong, came from Xianning in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，仕明為副將。

translations.literal: He was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and served the Ming as a vice general.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in riding and archery, he had served the Ming as a vice general.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，英親王阿濟格師次九江，勇來降，檄令招撫，得總兵以下七百餘人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, when the Prince of Ying, Ajige, halted his army at Jiujiang, Yong came to surrender; he was ordered by proclamation to win over and pacify troops, and obtained more than seven hundred men from regional commanders downward.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, when the Prince of Ying, Ajige, encamped at Jiujiang, Yong surrendered. Ordered to win over and pacify the enemy, he brought in more than seven hundred officers and men from the rank of regional commander down.

sentences.zh: 授游擊，隸陝西總督孟喬芳標下。

translations.literal: He was appointed guerrilla commander and placed under the banner of Shaanxi governor-general Meng Qiaofang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a guerrilla commander and assigned to the staff of Meng Qiaofang, governor-general of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時李自成將賀珍、賀弘器、李明義等分據漢中、興安、固原諸地，窺西安。

translations.literal: At the time Li Zicheng's generals He Zhen, He Hongqi, Li Mingyi, and others held Hanzhong, Xing'an, Guyuan, and other places separately, watching for an opening against Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Zicheng's generals He Zhen, He Hongqi, Li Mingyi, and others held Hanzhong, Xing'an, Guyuan, and neighboring districts and were threatening Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 勇與副將任珍、馬寧等禦戰，屢敗之。

translations.literal: Yong, together with vice generals Ren Zhen, Ma Ning, and others, met them in battle and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yong fought them alongside vice generals Ren Zhen and Ma Ning and defeated them again and again.

sentences.zh: 四年，寧夏叛將馬德結弘器陷安定，勇從總兵劉芳名率師赴援，戰，馬寧陣擒德，勇攻克固原，獲弘器、明義，誅之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Ningxia rebel Ma De joined with Hongqi and seized Anding; Yong followed regional commander Liu Fangming in leading troops to the relief, fought, Ma Ning captured De on the field, Yong stormed and took Guyuan, captured Hongqi and Mingyi, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the Ningxia rebel Ma De joined He Hongqi in taking Anding. Yong marched to the relief under regional commander Liu Fangming. In the fighting Ma Ning captured Ma De in battle, while Yong took Guyuan, seized He Hongqi and Li Mingyi, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 四年，米喇印、丁國棟以蘭州叛，陷臨洮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Mi Layin and Ding Guodong rebelled from Lanzhou and seized Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Mi Layin and Ding Guodong rose in rebellion at Lanzhou and captured Lintao.

sentences.zh: 勇與副將陳萬略率師夾擊，破賊，复臨洮。

translations.literal: Yong and vice general Chen Wanlue led troops in a pincer attack, broke the bandits, and recovered Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and vice general Chen Wanlue struck the rebels from two sides, routed them, and recovered Lintao.

sentences.zh: 逐賊至岷州，敗之宮堡，又敗之馬韓山。

translations.literal: Pursuing the bandits to Minzhou, he defeated them at Gongbao and again at Mahanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels to Minzhou, defeated them at Gongbao, and defeated them again at Mahanshan.

sentences.zh: 賊分竄二崖洞，殲焉；

translations.literal: The bandits scattered into two cliff caves and were annihilated there;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into two cliff caves and were wiped out there;

sentences.zh: 又敗之馬家坪，獲明延長王識駉。

translations.literal: he again defeated them at Majiaping and captured the Ming prince of Yanchang, Wang Shikun.
translations.idiomatic: he routed them again at Majiaping and captured Wang Shikun, the Ming prince of Yanchang.

sentences.zh: 喬芳攻拔蘭州，喇印、國棟走甘州。

translations.literal: Qiaofang stormed and took Lanzhou; Layin and Guodong fled to Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaofang stormed Lanzhou and took it, while Layin and Guodong fled to Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 勇等率師與喬芳會，遂渡河而西。

translations.literal: Yong and others led their troops to join Qiaofang, then crossed the river and marched west.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and his officers joined Qiaofang, crossed the river, and marched west.

sentences.zh: 八月，至甘州，賊出戰，屢擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they reached Ganzhou; the bandits came out to fight and were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they reached Ganzhou. The rebels came out to give battle and were beaten back again and again.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，總兵南一魁奪門入，勇入城巷戰，賊夜遁，逐之至北山，殲賊甚眾。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, regional commander Nan Yikui seized the gate and entered; Yong fought in the streets inside the city, the bandits fled by night, he pursued them to Beishan, and destroyed a great many of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year regional commander Nan Yikui forced the gate and entered the city. Yong fought house to house in the streets. The rebels fled by night; he pursued them to Beishan and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 斬喇印於水泉，國棟走肅州，師從之。

translations.literal: Layin was beheaded at Shuiquan; Guodong fled to Suzhou, and the army followed.
translations.idiomatic: Layin was beheaded at Shuiquan. Guodong fled to Suzhou, and the army pursued him.

sentences.zh: 五月，至肅州，伏壕外，伺賊出牧，擒斬，不使得入。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they reached Suzhou, lay in ambush outside the moat, waited for the bandits to come out to pasture, captured and killed them, and did not allow them to re-enter.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they reached Suzhou. Yong posted men outside the moat to ambush rebels who came out to graze their herds, seized and killed them, and kept them from re-entering the city.

sentences.zh: 十二月，勇與馬寧督兵樹雲梯登城，遂復肅州，誅國棟，超授甘肅總兵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Yong and Ma Ning directed troops to set up cloud ladders and scale the wall, then recovered Suzhou, executed Guodong, and Yong was promoted out of turn to regional commander of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yong and Ma Ning had siege ladders raised and stormed the walls. Suzhou was recovered, Guodong was executed, and Yong was promoted ahead of schedule to regional commander of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十年，敘功，授三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when merit was reviewed, he was granted the third-rank ada hahafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his services were recognized and he was granted the hereditary rank of third-class ada hahafan.

sentences.zh: 大學士洪承疇視師湖廣，勇請自效，詔獎其忠勤，召詣京師。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou inspected the army in Huguang; Yong asked to offer himself, an edict praised his loyalty and diligence, and he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou took command in Huguang, Yong volunteered for service. The court praised his loyalty and diligence and summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 承疇亦薦勇智勇兼備，所部兵精馬足，請移授經略右標總兵，上許之。

translations.literal: Chengchou also recommended that Yong combined wisdom and courage, that his troops were elite and his horses ample, and requested that he be transferred and appointed regional commander of the right banner of the field marshal; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou also recommended Yong as a man of both wisdom and valor whose troops were first-rate and well mounted, and asked that he be transferred to command the right banner of the field marshal's army. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 勇入對，賜冠服、甲胄、弓矢，加右都督。

translations.literal: Yong entered for audience, was granted court dress, armor, bow and arrows, and was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was received in audience, presented with court dress, armor, bow and arrows, and promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 勇移家京師，乞賜宅；

translations.literal: Yong moved his household to the capital and begged that a residence be granted;
translations.idiomatic: Yong moved his family to the capital and asked for a residence;

sentences.zh: 子云翥，以廕授陝西衛指揮，乞改隸京衛，並得旨俞允。

translations.literal: his son Yunzhu, appointed by yin privilege as commander of the Shaanxi guard, begged to be transferred to a capital guard, and both requests received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: his son Yunzhu, who held a hereditary appointment as commander of the Shaanxi guard, asked to be transferred to a capital guard. Both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 勇將行，命內大臣索尼等傳諭曰：「當今良將如勇者甚少。

translations.literal: As Yong was about to depart, the emperor ordered inner ministers such as Sonin to transmit his words: "Among the fine generals of today, men like Yong are very few.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yong departed, the emperor had inner ministers including Sonin convey this message: "Fine generals like Yong are rare in our day.

sentences.zh: 軍務不可懸度，當相機而行，勿負才輕敵。

translations.literal: Military affairs cannot be judged in advance; you should act as circumstances require, and must not rely on talent and despise the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: War cannot be planned in the abstract. Act as circumstances demand, and do not let your ability make you underestimate the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」至軍，佐承疇屢破敵。

translations.literal: When he reached the army, he assisted Chengchou in repeatedly defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the front he assisted Chengchou and helped win victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從徇貴州，明將羅大順焚新添衛，勇率兵馳戰，大順走十萬谿，勇與一魁等破其壘。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed in the pacification of Guizhou; the Ming general Luo Dashun burned Xintianwei, Yong led troops in a rapid attack, Dashun fled to Shiwanxi, and Yong with Yikui and others stormed his stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he took part in the campaign in Guizhou. The Ming general Luo Dashun burned Xintianwei. Yong rode hard to the fight; Dashun fled to Shiwanxi, and Yong with Yikui and others stormed his fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 復從信郡王多尼下雲南，次盤江。

translations.literal: He again followed the Prince of Xin, Duoni, south into Yunnan and halted at Panjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed the Prince of Xin, Duoni, into Yunnan and encamped at Panjiang.

sentences.zh: 明兵焚鐵索橋，勇夜督兵造梁，黎明，全軍皆得渡，破明將白文選於七星關。

translations.literal: Ming troops burned the iron-chain bridge; Yong by night directed troops to build a span, and at dawn the whole army was able to cross; he defeated the Ming general Bai Wenxuan at Qixing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ming forces burned the iron-chain bridge. Yong had his men build a crossing by night, and at dawn the entire army was across. He then defeated the Ming general Bai Wenxuan at Qixing Pass.

sentences.zh: 十六年，加左都督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十七年，命移鎮臨元、廣西諸處。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was ordered to transfer his garrison to Linyuan, Guangxi, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was ordered to take up command at Linyuan, Guangxi, and neighboring posts.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷雲南提督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to provincial military commander of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed provincial military commander of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，以勇久鎮甘肅，威名素著，屬番讋服，命還鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, because Yong had long garrisoned Gansu, his renown was already established, and the dependent tribes were in awe and submission, he was ordered to return and garrison Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi, because Yong had long commanded Gansu, where his fame had made the frontier tribes submit in awe, he was ordered back to that post.

sentences.zh: 三年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 西喇塔拉饒水草，號大草灘，厄魯特蒙古乞駐牧於此。

translations.literal: Xilatala was rich in water and grass and was called Dacaotan; the Oirat Mongols begged to pasture there.
translations.idiomatic: Xilatala, known as Dacaotan, was rich pastureland, and the Oirat Mongols asked permission to graze there.

sentences.zh: 勇以其地當要隘，不容逼處，自往諭之，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Yong, because the place was a strategic pass and could not tolerate their pressing close, went in person to instruct them, and the matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Yong judged the place a vital pass where they could not be allowed to crowd in. He went in person to warn them off, and the matter ended there.

sentences.zh: 因請築城其地，曰永固。

translations.literal: He therefore requested that a city be built there, called Yonggu.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to build a fortress there, which was named Yonggu.

sentences.zh: 旁建八寨，相聯屬為聲勢。

translations.literal: Eight stockades were built nearby, linked together to form a combined show of force.
translations.idiomatic: Eight outposts were built nearby and linked together to extend his defensive reach.

sentences.zh: 四年，蒙古徙牧近邊，請增西寧兵四千五百二十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, as the Mongols moved their pastures close to the border, he requested an increase of 4,520 troops at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, as Mongols moved their herds close to the border, he asked for 4,520 additional troops at Xining.

sentences.zh: 部議下總督覆覈，上特命允之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and referred it to the governor-general for review; the emperor specially ordered that it be approved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry referred the request to the governor-general for review, but the emperor personally ordered it approved.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吳三桂反，四川總兵吳之茂叛應之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rebelled, and Sichuan regional commander Wu Zhimao rebelled in response.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rebelled, and Wu Zhimao, regional commander of Sichuan, rose in support.

sentences.zh: 十三年，三桂使招勇，勇執其使以聞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Sangui sent envoys to win Yong over; Yong seized the envoys and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Sangui sent envoys to win him over. Yong seized the envoys and reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 陝西提督王輔臣亦叛，勇督兵防禦。

translations.literal: Shaanxi provincial commander Wang Fuchen also rebelled, and Yong directed troops in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuchen, provincial commander of Shaanxi, rebelled as well, and Yong took command of the defense.

sentences.zh: 十四年，巡撫華善疏言：「輔臣遙應三桂，西番土回乘隙並起，河西危甚，得免淪陷，皆勇之力。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Grand Coordinator Hua Shan memorialized: "Fuchen responds to Sangui from afar; the western tribes and Muslim communities have risen together at the opening, the Hexi region is in grave danger, and that it has escaped collapse is entirely due to Yong's power.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Grand Coordinator Hua Shan memorialized: "Fuchen coordinates with Sangui from afar, while western tribes and Muslim communities have risen together at the first opportunity. The Hexi region was in grave peril; that it did not fall is entirely Yong's doing.

sentences.zh: 請敕許勇便宜。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict authorize Yong to act at discretion."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be authorized by edict to act at his own discretion."

sentences.zh: 」命授靖逆將軍，仍領提督，總兵以下聽指揮。

translations.literal: He was ordered appointed Pacification General, still retaining the provincial command, and all from regional commander downward were to obey his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was appointed Pacification General while retaining his post as provincial commander; all officers from regional commander down were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 輔臣招勇，勇斬其使，上嘉之，封靖逆侯。

translations.literal: Fuchen tried to win Yong over; Yong beheaded his envoy; the emperor praised this and enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Pacifies Rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuchen tried to win him over, Yong executed the envoy. The emperor commended him and enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Pacifies Rebels.

sentences.zh: 勇遣西寧總兵王進寶率師攻蘭州。

translations.literal: Yong sent Xining regional commander Wang Jinbao to lead troops in an attack on Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent Wang Jinbao, regional commander of Xining, to attack Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 輔臣將潘瑀攻洮州，曾文耀攻河州，番部乘隙肆掠。

translations.literal: Fuchen's generals Pan Yu attacked Taozhou and Zeng Wenyao attacked Hezhou, while tribal groups seized the opening to plunder freely.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen's generals Pan Yu attacked Taozhou and Zeng Wenyao attacked Hezhou, while frontier tribes took advantage of the turmoil to raid at will.

sentences.zh: 勇率兵攻河州，文耀敗走。

translations.literal: Yong led troops to attack Hezhou; Wenyao was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yong marched on Hezhou and put Wenyao to flight.

sentences.zh: 別遣土官楊朝梁攻洮州，自督兵繼其後，瑀亦敗走。

translations.literal: He separately sent native official Yang Chaoliang to attack Taozhou and himself directed troops to follow after; Yu was also defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the native official Yang Chaoliang against Taozhou and followed with his main force; Pan Yu was defeated and fled as well.

sentences.zh: 上嘉勇謀略，以其次子云翼為太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Yong's strategy and appointed his second son Yunyi as Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Yong's strategy and appointed his second son Yunyi director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 勇進攻鞏昌，輔臣將任國治等潛師入城，與城兵共出戰。

translations.literal: Yong advanced to attack Gongchang; Fuchen's generals Ren Guozhi and others secretly led troops into the city and came out to fight together with the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Yong advanced on Gongchang. Fuchen's generals Ren Guozhi and others slipped reinforcements into the city and sallied out with the garrison.

sentences.zh: 勇與副將劉宣聖等奮擊，截其歸路，斬馘過半，獲四百七十三人。

translations.literal: Yong with vice generals Liu Xuansheng and others fought fiercely, cut off their line of retreat, killed and wounded more than half, and captured 473 men.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and vice generals including Liu Xuansheng fought hard, cut off their retreat, killed more than half the enemy, and took 473 prisoners.

sentences.zh: 時輔臣據平涼，貝勒洞鄂督兵圍攻，久不下，上命勇率師會之。

translations.literal: At the time Fuchen held Pingliang; the beile Tong'e directed troops in a siege but could not take it for a long time; the emperor ordered Yong to lead troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen held Pingliang, where the beile Tong'e had long besieged him without success. The emperor ordered Yong to bring his army to join the siege.

sentences.zh: 勇疏言鞏昌要地，兵力難分，下廷臣議，令勇固守鞏昌。

translations.literal: Yong memorialized that Gongchang was a vital place and that his forces could not be divided; the matter was referred to court ministers for deliberation, and Yong was ordered to hold Gongchang firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized that Gongchang was a vital post and that he could not spare troops. The court deliberated and ordered him to hold Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂遣其將吳之茂自四川北犯，為輔臣聲援，屯西和。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui sent his general Wu Zhimao to invade north from Sichuan in support of Fuchen, and he encamped at Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent his general Wu Zhimao north from Sichuan to support Fuchen, and Zhimao encamped at Xihe.

sentences.zh: 勇與振武將軍佛尼埒及進寶等御之，三戰皆勝。

translations.literal: Yong, together with the Pacifying Martial General Fonielie and Jinbao and others, met them and won all three battles.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, the Pacifying Martial General Fonielie, Jinbao, and others met them and won three battles in succession.

sentences.zh: 寧夏兵變，戕提督陳福。

translations.literal: The Ningxia troops mutinied and killed provincial commander Chen Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison at Ningxia mutinied and killed provincial commander Chen Fu.

sentences.zh: 勇還駐鞏昌，疏薦天津總兵趙良棟才勇，命即授寧夏提督。

translations.literal: Yong returned to garrison Gongchang and memorialized recommending Tianjin regional commander Zhao Liangdong for talent and courage; he was immediately appointed provincial commander of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Yong returned to Gongchang and recommended Zhao Liangdong, regional commander of Tianjin, as a man of talent and valor. Liangdong was immediately appointed provincial commander of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 十五年，敘复洮、河二州功，加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when merit for recovering Taozhou and Hezhou was reviewed, he was made Junior Guardian and concurrently Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year his success in recovering Taozhou and Hezhou was recognized, and he was made Junior Guardian and concurrently Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 吳之茂屯樂門，分兵攻陷通渭。

translations.literal: Wu Zhimao encamped at Lemen and sent detachments that stormed and took Tongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhimao was encamped at Lemen and sent detachments that captured Tongwei.

sentences.zh: 勇督兵道伏羌赴援，至十八盤坡，與之茂兵遇，張兩翼衝擊，之茂兵潰，乘勝复通渭。

translations.literal: Yong directed troops by way of Fuqiang to the relief; at Shibapanpo they met Zhimao's force, spread both wings in a charge, Zhimao's troops were routed, and taking advantage of victory they recovered Tongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yong marched to the relief by way of Fuqiang. At Shibapanpo he met Zhimao's force, charged with both wings extended, routed the enemy, and pressed on to recover Tongwei.

sentences.zh: 進攻樂門，之茂據險，列十一寨，勇度地，令橫營山梁。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Lemen, Zhimao held the difficult ground and arrayed eleven stockades; Yong surveyed the terrain and ordered camps laid out across the mountain ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Lemen, he found Zhimao holding difficult ground behind eleven stockades. Yong studied the terrain and had his men camp across the ridge.

sentences.zh: 營甫立，賊齊出，勇令兵持草一束，與都統赫葉分擊南北山梁，賊亦南北應戰。

translations.literal: As soon as the camps were set, the bandits all came out; Yong ordered the troops each to carry a bundle of straw, and with Commander-in-Chief Heye struck the northern and southern ridges separately; the bandits also responded north and south.
translations.idiomatic: The camps had barely been pitched when the rebels came out in force. Yong had each man carry a bundle of straw and, with Commander-in-Chief Heye, attacked the northern and southern ridges; the rebels met them on both fronts.

sentences.zh: 火器發，賊敗走入寨，兵投草填塹直進，殺賊千餘。

translations.literal: Firearms were discharged, the bandits were defeated and ran into the stockades, the troops threw straw to fill the ditches and advanced straight in, and killed more than a thousand bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the firearms opened fire the rebels broke and fled into their stockades. Yong's men threw straw into the ditches, pressed straight in, and killed more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 之茂收餘眾复戰，勇勒兵衝擊，之茂大敗。

translations.literal: Zhimao gathered his remaining troops and fought again; Yong marshaled his troops in a charge and Zhimao was heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhimao rallied his survivors and fought again, but Yong charged and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 勇與佛尼勒、進寶等盡平賊寨。

translations.literal: Yong, together with Foniele, Jinbao, and others, completely pacified the rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, Foniele, Jinbao, and the others then cleared every rebel stockade.

sentences.zh: 之茂夜走，追敗之牡丹園，又敗之西和北山，之茂僅以數騎遁。

translations.literal: Zhimao fled by night; they pursued and defeated him at Mudanyuan, defeated him again at Xibei Beishan, and Zhimao escaped with only a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhimao fled by night. They overtook and defeated him at Mudanyuan and again on Beishan west of Xihe; he escaped with only a handful of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 大學士圖海出視師，輔臣降，勇遣兵收平涼、慶陽、鞏昌諸屬縣。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Tu Hai went out to inspect the army; Fuchen surrendered, and Yong sent troops to recover Pingliang, Qingyang, Gongchang, and their subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Tu Hai took the field, Fuchen surrendered. Yong sent troops to recover Pingliang, Qingyang, Gongchang, and their dependent counties.

sentences.zh: 詔褒勇功，進一等侯，加少傅兼太子太師。

translations.literal: An edict praised Yong's merit; he was advanced to first-rank marquis and made Junior Mentor and concurrently Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his achievements, raised him to first-rank marquis, and made him Junior Mentor and concurrently Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十七年，準噶爾台吉噶爾丹兵入河套，厄魯特部為所敗，假道赴青海，闌入內地，勇驅令出塞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Zunghar taiji Galdan's troops entered the Ordos; the Oirat tribes were defeated by him, took a route toward Qinghai, forced their way into the interior, and Yong drove them out beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the Zunghar taiji Galdan invaded the Ordos. Defeated Oirat bands took the road toward Qinghai and crossed into Chinese territory; Yong drove them back beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，入覲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was received at court.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，以老病乞休，諭留之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, on grounds of age and illness he begged to retire; an edict ordered him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he asked to retire on account of age and illness, but the emperor ordered him to stay on.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，聞青海蒙古游牧近邊城，率兵赴丹山防禦，至甘州，病篤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, hearing that Qinghai Mongols were pasturing close to the border cities, he led troops to Danshan in defense; reaching Ganzhou, he fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, hearing that Qinghai Mongols were grazing close to the border towns, he led troops to Danshan. At Ganzhou his illness grew grave.

sentences.zh: 上聞，遣醫併其子云翼馳驛往視。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he sent a physician together with his son Yunyi by relay post to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the emperor sent a physician and his son Yunyi by relay posthorses to attend him.

sentences.zh: 尋率，贈少師仍兼太子太師，賜祭葬，諡襄壯。

translations.literal: Soon after he died; he was posthumously made Junior Preceptor and still concurrently Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, granted the rites of sacrifice and burial, and given the posthumous title Xiangzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after. He was posthumously made Junior Preceptor and still concurrently Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, granted state funeral honors, and given the posthumous title Xiangzhuang.

sentences.zh: 勇身經數百戰，克府五、州縣五十，右足中流矢，傷骨，不能履，常以肩輿督戰。

translations.literal: Yong personally passed through several hundred battles, took five prefectures and fifty districts and counties, was struck in the right foot by a flying arrow that injured the bone so that he could not walk, and often directed battles from a sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had fought in several hundred battles, taken five prefectures and fifty districts and counties, and been struck in the right foot by an arrow that shattered the bone and left him unable to walk. He often directed battles from a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 臨敵若無事，而智計橫出，每以寡勝眾。

translations.literal: Facing the enemy he was as if at ease, yet stratagems poured forth, and he often overcame the many with the few.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he seemed unhurried, yet stratagems poured from him, and he often defeated larger forces with smaller ones.

sentences.zh: 居恆恂恂退讓，賓禮賢士。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he was respectful and yielding, and received worthy men as guests with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he was modest and courteous and treated men of talent with honor.

sentences.zh: 用人盡其材，其所甄拔，往往起卒伍為大將，良棟、進寶尤其著者也。

translations.literal: In employing men he used their full talent; those he selected and promoted often rose from the ranks to become great generals, Liangdong and Jinbao being especially notable.
translations.idiomatic: He used every man's gifts to the full. Many he raised from the ranks became great generals, Liangdong and Jinbao foremost among them.

sentences.zh: 子云翼，襲爵，官至江南提督。

translations.literal: His son Yunyi inherited the title and rose to provincial military commander of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yunyi inherited the title and rose to provincial military commander of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡恪定。

translations.literal: When he died he was given the posthumous title Keding.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received the posthumous title Keding.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，祀勇賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period Yong was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongzheng emperor he was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十三年，命以一等侯世襲罔替。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Qianlong he was ordered to pass down the first-rank marquisate in perpetual inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year of Qianlong his descendants were granted perpetual inheritance of the first-rank marquisate.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，詔褒勇、良棟、進寶勳績，尤稱勇有古名將風。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year an edict praised the achievements of Yong, Liangdong, and Jinbao, especially calling Yong one who had the air of the great generals of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year an edict praised the achievements of Yong, Liangdong, and Jinbao, singling out Yong as a man in the mold of the great generals of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 時勇四世孫承勳襲爵，以散秩大臣曠班，降三等侍衛，命復還散秩大臣。

translations.literal: At the time Yong's fourth-generation descendant Cheng Xun inherited the title; because as a minister without portfolio he had been absent from duty, he was reduced to third-rank bodyguard, then ordered restored to minister without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's fourth-generation descendant Cheng Xun then held the title. Having been absent from duty as a minister without portfolio, he was demoted to third-rank bodyguard, then restored to minister without portfolio by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 趙良棟，字擎宇，甘肅寧夏人，先世居榆林。

translations.literal: Zhao Liangdong, style name Qingyu, was a native of Ningxia in Gansu; his forebears had dwelt in Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangdong, whose style name was Qingyu, came from Ningxia in Gansu. His family had originally lived in Yulin.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，師定陝西，良棟應募，隸總督孟喬芳標下，檄署潼關守備。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, when the army pacified Shaanxi, Liangdong enlisted, was placed under Governor-General Meng Qiaofang's banner, and was ordered by proclamation to act as Tongguan garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, when the army pacified Shaanxi, Liangdong enlisted and joined Meng Qiaofang's staff. He was ordered to serve as acting commander of the Tongguan garrison.

sentences.zh: 從征秦州、鞏昌，擊敗叛將賀珍、武大定。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns in Qinzhou and Gongchang and defeated the rebel generals He Zhen and Wu Dading.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Qinzhou and Gongchang and defeated the rebel generals He Zhen and Wu Dading.

sentences.zh: 授寧夏水利屯田都司。

translations.literal: He was appointed colonel of Ningxia's waterworks and military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed colonel in charge of Ningxia's irrigation colonies.

sentences.zh: 五年，討河西回，擒丁國棟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, in the campaign against the Hexi Muslims, Ding Guodong was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, during the campaign against the Hexi Muslims, Ding Guodong was captured.

sentences.zh: 良棟在行間，擢高台游擊。

translations.literal: Liangdong was in the ranks and was promoted to guerrilla commander of Gaotai.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong was in the field and was promoted to guerrilla commander of Gaotai.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以經略洪承疇薦，從征雲、貴，授督標中軍副將。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, on Field Marshal Hong Chengchou's recommendation, he followed the campaign in Yunnan and Guizhou and was appointed vice general of the field marshal's central army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, on Hong Chengchou's recommendation, he joined the Yunnan-Guizhou campaign and was made vice general of the field marshal's central army.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，擢雲南廣羅總兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he was promoted to regional commander of Guangluo in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he was promoted to regional commander of the Guangluo district in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 先後剿平馬乃、隴納、水西諸苗。

translations.literal: In succession he suppressed and pacified the Miao of Manai, Longna, Shuixi, and other regions.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he pacified the Miao of Manai, Longna, Shuixi, and other regions.

sentences.zh: 四年，移鎮貴州平遠，遭父喪，吳三桂以水西未大定，留勿遣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to command at Pingyuan in Guizhou; he suffered his father's death, but Wu Sangui, on the grounds that Shuixi was not yet fully pacified, detained him and would not let him go.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Pingyuan in Guizhou. When his father died, Wu Sangui refused to release him, citing the fact that Shuixi was not yet fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 良棟辭，忤三桂，同官為排解，乃得歸終制。

translations.literal: Liangdong declined and offended Sangui; fellow officials mediated on his behalf, and only then was he able to return home to observe the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong insisted on leaving, which offended Sangui, but colleagues interceded for him and he was at last allowed to go home and complete his mourning obligations.

sentences.zh: 八年，起山西大同總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was recalled to serve as regional commander at Datong in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled as regional commander at Datong in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，移鎮直隸天津。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to command at Tianjin in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Tianjin in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十二年，三桂反。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Sangui rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十三年，寧夏兵變，戕提督陳福。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Ningxia troops mutinied and killed Provincial Military Commissioner Chen Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Ningxia garrison mutinied and killed Provincial Military Commissioner Chen Fu.

sentences.zh: 甘肅提督張勇薦良棟，擢寧夏提督。

translations.literal: Gansu Provincial Military Commissioner Zhang Yong recommended Liangdong, and he was promoted to Ningxia Provincial Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong, provincial military commissioner of Gansu, recommended Liangdong, who was promoted to the same post at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 入覲，奏寧夏亂兵，宜誅首惡、宥脅從，上頷之。

translations.literal: On entering audience he memorialized that among the Ningxia mutineers the ringleaders should be executed and those coerced should be pardoned; the Emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: At court he argued that among the Ningxia mutineers only the ringleaders should be punished and the coerced men spared. The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 良棟請留孥京師，賜宅以居。

translations.literal: Liangdong asked to leave his wife and children in the capital, and a residence was granted for them to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong asked to leave his family in the capital, and the court granted them a house.

sentences.zh: 簡精兵百疾馳赴鎮，宣上諭撫慰。

translations.literal: He selected a hundred elite troops and galloped post-haste to his post, proclaiming the Emperor's edict of reassurance and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: He took a hundred picked men and rode at full speed to his command, proclaiming the Emperor's message of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 察知倡亂者把總劉德，而參將熊虎與其謀，戕福者營兵閻國賢、陳進忠。

translations.literal: On investigation he learned that platoon leader Liu De had instigated the revolt, that Vice Commander Xiong Hu had plotted with him, and that the camp soldiers Yan Guoxian and Chen Jinzhong had killed Fu.
translations.idiomatic: His investigation showed that platoon leader Liu De had started the mutiny with the help of Vice Commander Xiong Hu, while camp soldiers Yan Guoxian and Chen Jinzhong had killed Chen Fu.

sentences.zh: 乃分兵使出防，散其黨羽，逮虎等正其罪，請旨斬之。

translations.literal: He then divided his troops and sent them out on guard duty, scattered the conspirators' followers, arrested Hu and the others and judged their crimes, and requested imperial sanction to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: He deployed his forces on guard duty, broke up the conspirators' network, arrested Xiong Hu and his accomplices, tried them, and secured imperial approval for their execution.

sentences.zh: 是時大將軍圖海督師平涼，討王輔臣，良棟及平涼提督王進寶並聽指揮，分兵定秦州、西和、禮縣。

translations.literal: At this time Grand General Tu Hai directed the army at Pingliang to campaign against Wang Fuchen; Liangdong and Pingliang Provincial Military Commissioner Wang Jinbao both received his orders, and by dividing their forces they pacified Qinzhou, Xihe, and Lixian.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Tu Hai was then campaigning against Wang Fuchen from Pingliang. Liangdong and Wang Jinbao, provincial military commissioner of Pingliang, served under his command and sent detachments to secure Qinzhou, Xihe, and Lixian.

sentences.zh: 十八年，良棟疏言：「寧夏兵舊習驕縱，臣三年訓練，漸遵紀律，並嚴禁侵剋額餉，眾志思奮。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Liangdong memorialized, saying: "The Ningxia troops were formerly accustomed to arrogance and license; your servant has trained them for three years until they gradually observe discipline, and has strictly forbidden encroachment on allotted pay, so that the men's will is set on striving."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Liangdong wrote: "The Ningxia troops were once unruly and arrogant, but after three years of training they now keep discipline. I have also forbidden any skimming of their pay, and the men are eager to fight."

sentences.zh: 臣年漸老，不乘時努力，虛負上恩。

translations.literal: "Your servant grows old year by year; if I do not exert myself while the time is ripe, I shall have failed the Emperor's grace in vain."
translations.idiomatic: "I am growing old. If I do not seize this moment, I shall have wasted Your Majesty's trust."

sentences.zh: 今湖南既定，宜取漢中、興安，規四川。

translations.literal: "Now that Hunan is settled, we should take Hanzhong and Xing'an and plan for Sichuan."
translations.idiomatic: "Hunan is secure. We should take Hanzhong and Xing'an and aim at Sichuan."

sentences.zh: 臣原精選所部步騎五千，獨當一路。

translations.literal: "Your servant is willing to choose five thousand infantry and cavalry from his command and bear one route alone."
translations.idiomatic: "I am ready to take five thousand foot and horse from my own command and hold one route by myself."

sentences.zh: 」上覽奏嘉許，下圖海。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial with approval and transmitted it to Tu Hai.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial with approval and forwarded it to Tu Hai.

sentences.zh: 圖海議先破棧道、益門鎮諸處賊壘，分四道進取；

translations.literal: Tu Hai proposed first breaking the rebel stockades at the plank road, Yimen town, and other places, and advancing in four columns;
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai proposed first storming the rebel strongholds along the plank road, at Yimen town, and elsewhere, then advancing in four columns.

sentences.zh: 而涼州提督孫思克疏請緩師，得旨切責。

translations.literal: but Liangzhou Provincial Military Commissioner Sun Sike memorialized asking to delay the campaign and received an edict sharply rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sike, provincial military commissioner of Liangzhou, had meanwhile asked to slow the advance and was sharply rebuked by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 乃以十月定師期，良棟將所部出徽縣。

translations.literal: The campaign date was then fixed for the tenth month, and Liangdong led his troops out from Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: The army was ordered to move in the tenth month, and Liangdong marched out of Huixian with his division.

sentences.zh: 師進破密樹關，遣兵襲黃渚關分敵勢，大戰，破三桂兵，克徽縣。

translations.literal: The army advanced and broke Mishu Pass, sent troops to strike Huangzhu Pass and divide the enemy's strength, fought a great battle, defeated Sangui's troops, and took Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: His forces broke Mishu Pass, sent a detachment against Huangzhu Pass to split the enemy, fought a major battle, routed Wu Sangui's army, and captured Huixian.

sentences.zh: 思克出略陽，方次階州。

translations.literal: Sike came out through Lueyang and was just then encamped at Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sike had marched out through Lueyang and was encamped at Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 良棟師自徽縣進克略陽，三桂將吳之茂敗走。

translations.literal: Liangdong's army advanced from Huixian and took Lueyang; Sangui's general Wu Zhimao was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong advanced from Huixian and took Lueyang, driving off Wu Sangui's general Wu Zhimao.

sentences.zh: 良棟復進取陽平關，徇沔縣。

translations.literal: Liangdong again advanced to take Yangping Pass and pushed on to Mianxian.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong pressed on to Yangping Pass and swept through Mianxian.

sentences.zh: 進寶出鳳縣定漢中，良棟與會師寧羌，各奏捷。

translations.literal: Jinbao came out through Fengxian and secured Hanzhong; Liangdong joined him at Ningqiang, and each reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jinbao marched out through Fengxian and secured Hanzhong. Liangdong joined him at Ningqiang, and both reported victories.

sentences.zh: 授良棟勇略將軍，仍領寧夏提督。

translations.literal: Liangdong was appointed Brave Strategist General while still retaining the post of Ningxia Provincial Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong was made Brave Strategist General while continuing to hold the Ningxia command.

sentences.zh: 十九年，良棟與進寶分道進次白水壩，三桂兵夾江而陣，江水方漲，不得舟，賊矢石如雨。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Liangdong and Jinbao advanced by separate routes and halted at Baishuiba; Sangui's troops drew up on both banks of the river, the water was then in flood and boats could not be used, and rebel arrows and stones fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Liangdong and Jinbao advanced by separate routes to Baishuiba. Wu Sangui's troops lined both banks of the river. The water was high, there were no boats, and enemy arrows and stones poured down like rain.

sentences.zh: 良棟令於眾曰：「視我鞭所向，敢退者斬！

translations.literal: Liangdong ordered before the host, saying: "Watch where my whip points—whoever dares retreat shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong called out to his men: "Watch where my whip points. Anyone who retreats will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 」一軍皆奮呼。

translations.literal: The whole army shouted in exultation.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army roared in response.

sentences.zh: 良棟擐甲，驟馬亂流而渡，師從之，敵發砲，傷數十人，無回顧者。

translations.literal: Liangdong donned armor, spurred his horse through the swirling current and crossed; the army followed him. The enemy fired cannon and wounded several tens of men, yet not one looked back.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong put on armor, spurred his horse into the churning current, and crossed. His men followed. The enemy opened fire with cannon and wounded dozens, but not a man turned back.

sentences.zh: 三桂兵錯愕奔潰，逐之過青川，敗之石峽溝，再敗之青箐山，下龍安府，渡明月江，經綿竹。

translations.literal: Sangui's troops, startled and dismayed, broke and fled; he pursued them past Qingchuan, defeated them at Shixiagou, defeated them again at Qingqingshan, took Long'an Prefecture, crossed the Mingyue River, and passed through Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's troops broke in confusion. Liangdong pursued them past Qingchuan, routed them at Shixiagou and again at Qingqingshan, took Long'an Prefecture, crossed the Mingyue River, and marched through Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 三桂兵盡潰，所置巡撫張文德及其將汪文元等皆降，遂復成都，蓋出師甫十日。

translations.literal: Sangui's troops were wholly routed; the governor he had appointed, Zhang Wende, and his generals Wang Wenyuan and others all surrendered, and Chengdu was then recovered—it had been only ten days since the army set out.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's army collapsed completely. The governor he had installed, Zhang Wende, and generals such as Wang Wenyuan all surrendered, and Chengdu was recovered only ten days after the campaign began.

sentences.zh: 上獎良棟功，擢雲貴總督，加兵部尚書，仍領將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor rewarded Liangdong's merit, promoted him to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou, added the title Minister of War, and let him still hold the rank of general.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rewarded his achievement by making him governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, conferring the title of Minister of War, and allowing him to retain his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 良棟念寧夏當有代者，鎮兵且不能從征，疏辭總督，上弗許。

translations.literal: Liangdong reflected that Ningxia ought to have a replacement and that the garrison troops could not follow the campaign; he memorialized declining the governorship, but the Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong felt that Ningxia needed a new commander and that its garrison could not march with him. He asked to be relieved of the governorship, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 部議寧夏改設總兵，上即授良棟子廕生弘燦，仍將鎮兵從征。

translations.literal: The ministry proposed changing Ningxia to a regional-commander post; the Emperor at once appointed Liangdong's yin-privilege son Hongcan and still had the garrison troops follow the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommended replacing the Ningxia provincial command with a regional command. The Emperor immediately appointed Liangdong's yin-privilege son Hongcan and ordered the Ningxia garrison to continue on campaign.

sentences.zh: 時進寶亦克保寧，與建威將軍吳丹等徇順慶、重慶、遵義，皆下。

translations.literal: At this time Jinbao also took Baoning, and together with Establishing Might General Wu Dan and others advanced on Shunqing, Chongqing, and Zunyi—all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Jinbao had taken Baoning and, with Establishing Might General Wu Dan and others, swept Shunqing, Chongqing, and Zunyi, all of which fell.

sentences.zh: 良棟分遣游擊冶國用等西徇雅州，复象嶺、建昌諸衛。

translations.literal: Liangdong detached guerrilla commander Ye Guoyong and others to advance west against Yazhou, recovering Xiangling, Jianchang, and the other guards.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong sent guerrilla commander Ye Guoyong and others west against Yazhou and recovered Xiangling, Jianchang, and the other guard posts.

sentences.zh: 東略敘州，定納溪、永寧諸縣。

translations.literal: To the east he overran Xuzhou and secured Naxi, Yongning, and the other counties.
translations.idiomatic: To the east he overran Xuzhou and secured Naxi, Yongning, and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 疏請敕陝西、四川督撫諸臣合籌運餉濟軍。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that the governors and provincial commissioners of Shaanxi and Sichuan be ordered jointly to plan transport of provisions to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the throne to order the governors and commissioners of Shaanxi and Sichuan to coordinate grain shipments for the army.

sentences.zh: 師自四川分道：一自保寧出永寧，達霑益；

translations.literal: The army from Sichuan was to divide into routes: one from Baoning through Yongning to reach Zhan Yi;
translations.idiomatic: The forces in Sichuan would advance in two columns: one from Baoning through Yongning to Zhan Yi,

sentences.zh: 一自成都出建昌，達武定。

translations.literal: one from Chengdu through Jianchang to reach Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: and one from Chengdu through Jianchang to Wuding.

sentences.zh: 並下雲南。

translations.literal: Both were to descend on Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Both would then descend on Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 上韙其言，諭諸將帥協謀定策。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and instructed the generals to consult together and settle the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor endorsed the plan and told the commanders to coordinate their strategy.

sentences.zh: 尋議吳丹出永寧，良棟出建昌。

translations.literal: Soon it was decided that Wu Dan should advance from Yongning and Liangdong from Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon decided that Wu Dan would advance from Yongning and Liangdong from Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 吳世璠遣其將胡國柱、夏國相等攻陷永寧，犯瀘州、敘州，复聚窺建昌。

translations.literal: Wu Shifan sent his generals Hu Guozhu, Xia Guoxiang, and others to attack and seize Yongning, invade Luzhou and Xuzhou, and again gather forces to watch for an opening at Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan sent Hu Guozhu, Xia Guoxiang, and other generals to take Yongning and strike Luzhou and Xuzhou, then massed again to threaten Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 良棟檄總兵硃衣客將八千人援建昌，硃衣客戰不勝，退駐雅州。

translations.literal: Liangdong issued orders to Regional Commander Zhu Yike to lead eight thousand men to relieve Jianchang; Zhu Yike fought without victory and withdrew to encamp at Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong ordered Regional Commander Zhu Yike to relieve Jianchang with eight thousand men. Zhu Yike was defeated and fell back to Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 建昌守兵食盡，棄城走。

translations.literal: The defending troops at Jianchang exhausted their food, abandoned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianchang garrison ran out of food, abandoned the city, and fled.

sentences.zh: 良棟劾吳丹擁兵不進，致永寧陷賊，並及硃衣客引退狀，詔解吳丹將軍以授佛尼埒，逮硃衣客下刑部。

translations.literal: Liangdong impeached Wu Dan for holding his troops back without advancing, causing Yongning to fall to the rebels, and also cited Zhu Yike's withdrawal; an edict removed Wu Dan from his generalship and gave it to Funiye, and Zhu Yike was arrested and sent to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong accused Wu Dan of holding back his troops, which had led to the loss of Yongning, and reported Zhu Yike's retreat. An edict stripped Wu Dan of his command and gave it to Funiye, and Zhu Yike was arrested and sent to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 二十年，良棟率師次朝天關，遣弘燦出馬湖繞賊兵後，戰鳳凰村，再戰觀音崖。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Liangdong led his army to halt at Chaotian Pass, sent Hongcan out through Mahu to circle behind the rebel army, and fought at Fenghuang Village and again at Guanyin Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Liangdong encamped at Chaotian Pass and sent Hongcan through Mahu to strike the enemy rear. They fought at Fenghuang Village and again at Guanyin Cliff.

sentences.zh: 賊據崖，弘燦督兵攀崖襲其後，馘三百，俘八十餘。

translations.literal: The rebels held the cliff; Hongcan directed the troops to climb the cliff and strike their rear, taking three hundred heads and more than eighty prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the heights. Hongcan led his men up the cliff to attack from behind, killing three hundred and taking more than eighty prisoners.

sentences.zh: 令總兵李芳述、偏圖等逐至黃茅岡，賊分三道拒戰，弘燦分兵應之，自旦至暮，大破賊，斬其將沈明、張文祥，國柱等遁走。

translations.literal: He ordered Regional Commander Li Fangshu, Piantu, and others to pursue to Huangmaogang; the rebels divided into three routes to resist, Hongcan divided his forces to meet them, and from dawn to dusk he routed the rebels, beheading their generals Shen Ming and Zhang Wenxiang; Guozhu and the others fled.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Regional Commander Li Fangshu and Piantu in pursuit to Huangmaogang. The rebels met them in three columns. Hongcan divided his force to answer them and, fighting from dawn to dusk, routed the enemy, killing the generals Shen Ming and Zhang Wenxiang. Hu Guozhu and the others escaped.

sentences.zh: 复瀘州、敘州，遂克永寧，徇榮經。

translations.literal: He recovered Luzhou and Xuzhou, then took Yongning and advanced on Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Luzhou and Xuzhou, took Yongning, and pushed on into Rongjing.

sentences.zh: 良棟與會師夾江，克雅州，進復建昌。

translations.literal: Liangdong joined the converging armies on both banks of the river, took Yazhou, and advanced to recover Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong joined the converging columns on both banks of the river, took Yazhou, and advanced to recover Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 渡金沙江，次武定。

translations.literal: They crossed the Jinsha River and halted at Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Jinsha River and halted at Wuding.

sentences.zh: 大將軍貝子彰泰統湖廣、廣西諸路滿、漢兵四十萬下雲南，攻會城，屯城東歸化寺，西亙碧雞關，連營四十里，前臨昆明湖，湖中不設兵。

translations.literal: Grand General the Beile Zhang Zhangtai commanded four hundred thousand Manchu and Han troops from the routes of Huguang and Guangxi down into Yunnan, attacked the provincial capital, encamped at Guihua Temple east of the city, stretched west across Biji Pass in linked camps for forty li, faced Kunming Lake in front, and posted no troops on the lake.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Beile Zhang Zhangtai led four hundred thousand Manchu and Han troops from Huguang and Guangxi into Yunnan and besieged the capital. His camp lay east of the city at Guihua Temple, his line ran west along Biji Pass for forty li, and his front faced Kunming Lake—yet he posted no troops on the water.

sentences.zh: 世璠收餘眾固守，自水道轉運，相持數月未下。

translations.literal: Shifan gathered his remaining troops to hold fast, transported supplies by water routes, and the stalemate lasted several months without the city falling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan gathered his remaining forces for a stubborn defense and supplied them by water. The siege dragged on for months without success.

sentences.zh: 九月，良棟至軍，周視營壘，請於彰泰曰：「我師不速戰，相持日久，糧不繼，何以自存？

translations.literal: In the ninth month Liangdong reached the army, inspected the camps all around, and said to Zhang Zhangtai: "If our army does not fight quickly and the stalemate drags on, provisions will not last—how are we to survive?"
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liangdong reached the front, inspected the camps, and said to Zhang Zhangtai: "If we do not attack soon, this long standoff will exhaust our grain. How can we hold out?"

sentences.zh: 」彰泰曰：「皇上豢養滿洲兵，豈可輕進委之於敵？

translations.literal: Zhang Zhangtai said: "The Emperor maintains the Manchu troops at great expense—how can they be lightly sent forward and left to the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhangtai replied: "The Emperor maintains the Banner troops at great expense. How can we lightly throw them into the enemy's hands?"

sentences.zh: 且爾兵初來，亦宜體養，何可令其傷損？

translations.literal: "Moreover, your troops have only just arrived and ought to be rested and nurtured—how can they be made to suffer losses?"
translations.idiomatic: "Besides, your men have only just arrived. They need rest. Why should we let them be wasted?"

sentences.zh: 」良棟不從，率所部夜攻南壩，破壘奪橋，遂薄城。

translations.literal: Liangdong would not obey; he led his own troops in a night attack on Nanba, broke the stockade and seized the bridge, and then pressed close to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong would not listen. That night he led his own troops against Nanba, stormed the stockade, seized the bridge, and pressed up to the walls.

sentences.zh: 彰泰語良棟：「爾兵攻已瘁，宜暫退，令總督蔡毓榮代守。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhangtai said to Liangdong: "Your troops are worn out from attacking; you should withdraw for the moment and let Governor-General Cai Yurong hold the ground in your place."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhangtai told Liangdong: "Your men are exhausted from the assault. Pull back for now and let Governor-General Cai Yurong hold what you have taken."

sentences.zh: 」良棟曰：「我兵死戰所得地，奈何令他人守乎？

translations.literal: Liangdong said: "Ground my men won by fighting to the death—how can it be handed to others to guard?"
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong answered: "My men won this ground at the cost of their lives. Why should someone else hold it for us?"

sentences.zh: 」於是彰泰令諸軍悉進，世璠兵出城，戰於桂花寺，諸軍皆奮鬥，世璠兵大敗，乃自殺，餘眾以城降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Zhangtai ordered all the armies to advance together; Shifan's troops came out of the city and fought at Guihua Temple; every army fought fiercely; Shifan's troops were utterly defeated, whereupon he killed himself, and the remainder surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhangtai then ordered a general advance. Wu Shifan's troops came out and fought at Guihua Temple. Every column threw itself into the battle. Wu Shifan's army was routed, he killed himself, and the survivors surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 雲南平。

translations.literal: Yunnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 自三桂鎮雲南，至世璠覆亡，歷年久，子女玉帛充積饒富。

translations.literal: From the time Sangui held Yunnan until Shifan's overthrow, many years had passed, and children, jade, and silks had been heaped up in overflowing abundance.
translations.idiomatic: From Wu Sangui's rule in Yunnan to Wu Shifan's fall, many years had passed, and the rebel court had amassed wives, treasure, and silks in great profusion.

sentences.zh: 城破，諸將爭取之，獨良棟無所取，戢所部兵絲毫毋敢犯。

translations.literal: When the city fell the generals scrambled to seize the goods, but Liangdong alone took nothing and restrained his troops so that not the slightest thing was dared to be violated.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the other generals scrambled for loot, but Liangdong took nothing and kept his men under such strict discipline that not even the smallest item was touched.

sentences.zh: 硃衣客就逮，具疏辨，謂良棟與兵少，又無後應，是以退還。

translations.literal: When Zhu Yike was arrested he submitted a full memorial in his defense, saying that Liangdong had given him too few troops and no support from the rear, and that for this reason he had withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Yike was arrested he submitted a defense, claiming that Liangdong had given him too few men and no rear support, which was why he had retreated.

sentences.zh: 進寶亦疏謂建昌之陷，罪在良棟。

translations.literal: Jinbao also memorialized that for the fall of Jianchang the blame lay with Liangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Jinbao also wrote that Liangdong was to blame for the loss of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 良棟复劾硃衣客欺飾狡辨，且謂辨疏出進寶。

translations.literal: Liangdong again impeached Zhu Yike for deceit, concealment, and crafty argument, and further said that the defense memorial had come from Jinbao.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong in turn accused Zhu Yike of lying and evasion, and claimed that Jinbao had ghostwritten the defense.

sentences.zh: 上以軍事急，命俟事平察議。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because military affairs were urgent, ordered that investigation and judgment wait until the campaign was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Because the war was still urgent, the Emperor ordered that the case be reviewed only after the fighting ended.

sentences.zh: 雲南既定，召良棟詣京師，進寶亦入覲，諭曰：「當賊據漢中負固，諸將咸謂恢復為難，獨良棟首發議進剿，與進寶同取漢中。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was settled, Liangdong was summoned to the capital and Jinbao also entered audience; the Emperor instructed them, saying: "When the rebels held Hanzhong in stubborn defense, all the generals said recovery would be difficult; only Liangdong was first to propose advancing to attack, and together with Jinbao he took Hanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan was secured, Liangdong was summoned to court and Jinbao was received in audience. The Emperor told them: "When the rebels held Hanzhong, every general said recovery would be hard. Only Liangdong was first to urge an advance, and he and Jinbao together retook Hanzhong."

sentences.zh: 嗣因意見不相合，遂分道克成都，而進寶亦取保寧。

translations.literal: "Later, because your views did not agree, you took separate routes and took Chengdu, while Jinbao also took Baoning."
translations.idiomatic: "Later you quarreled and marched separately. Liangdong took Chengdu while Jinbao took Baoning."

sentences.zh: 成都不下，保寧未易拔；

translations.literal: "If Chengdu would not fall, Baoning would not be easy to storm;"
translations.idiomatic: "Chengdu could not be taken while Baoning held out;"

sentences.zh: 保寧不下，成都未易守：是二將並有功也。

translations.literal: "if Baoning would not fall, Chengdu would not be easy to hold: thus both generals have merit."
translations.idiomatic: "and Baoning could not be reduced while Chengdu remained in rebel hands. Both of you therefore deserve credit."

sentences.zh: 時賊皆入川抗戰，我師乘虛自沅州、鎮遠取貴陽，川中寇复張，已復之疆土幾至再陷，則二將不能和衷之所致也。

translations.literal: "At the time the rebels had all entered Sichuan to resist, our army took advantage of the opening to seize Guiyang from Yuanzhou and Zhenyuan, but the bandits in Sichuan revived and territory already recovered nearly fell again—this was caused by the two generals' inability to work in harmony."
translations.idiomatic: "While the rebels were fighting in Sichuan, our forces seized Guiyang from Yuanzhou and Zhenyuan. But the rebels in Sichuan rallied again, and territory we had recovered nearly fell a second time. That was because you two could not cooperate."

sentences.zh: 二將不諳大體，私忿攻訐。

translations.literal: "The two generals did not understand the larger interest and attacked each other out of private resentment."
translations.idiomatic: "You failed to see the larger interest and attacked each other out of private spite."

sentences.zh: 朕念其功績並茂，惟欲保全，互訐章奏，皆置不問，但論失援建昌罪。

translations.literal: "We, mindful that their achievements are both abundant, wished only to preserve them; the mutual impeachment memorials are all set aside without inquiry, and only the crime of failing to relieve Jianchang is to be judged."
translations.idiomatic: "I value both your records and mean to preserve you. I set aside your mutual accusations and judge only the failure to relieve Jianchang."

sentences.zh: 」部議硃衣客論斬，吳丹奪官籍沒，良棟奪官。

translations.literal: The ministry proposed that Zhu Yike be sentenced to decapitation, that Wu Dan be stripped of office and his household registers confiscated, and that Liangdong be deprived of office.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommended execution for Zhu Yike, stripping and confiscation for Wu Dan, and dismissal for Liangdong.

sentences.zh: 上命硃衣客免死為奴，吳丹奪官，良棟改授鑾儀使。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zhu Yike spared from death and made a bondservant, Wu Dan deprived of office, and Liangdong transferred to the post of Director of Imperial Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor spared Zhu Yike's life and made him a bondservant, stripped Wu Dan of office, and reassigned Liangdong as Director of Imperial Equipage.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，良棟疏陳戰功，請察議，下王大臣等議：良棟失建昌，以功抵罪；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Liangdong memorialized setting forth his battle achievements and asking for investigation and judgment; the matter was referred to the princes and grand ministers for deliberation: Liangdong had lost Jianchang, but his merit offset the crime;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Liangdong listed his battle honors and asked for a formal review. The case went to the princes and grand ministers, who ruled that the loss of Jianchang was offset by his achievements.

sentences.zh: 止敘從征將士弘燦、芳述、偏圖，並加左都督。

translations.literal: only the campaign generals Hongcan, Fangshu, and Piantu were to be rewarded, each promoted to Left Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Only the officers who had marched with him—Hongcan, Fangshu, and Piantu—were rewarded, each promoted to Left Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 良棟尋乞病歸。

translations.literal: Liangdong soon asked leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong soon asked to retire on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，上念良棟克雲南，廉潔守法紀，復將軍、總督原銜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Emperor, recalling that Liangdong had taken Yunnan and had been incorrupt and observant of law and discipline, restored his former titles of general and governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the Emperor, remembering Liangdong's conquest of Yunnan and his integrity, restored his former ranks as general and governor-general.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，入覲，復自陳戰功，上命還裡牒部具奏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he entered audience, again set forth his battle achievements himself, and the Emperor ordered that on his return home he send a memorial to the ministry for full presentation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he came to court, again pleaded his battle record, and the Emperor told him to submit a full memorial through the ministry after he returned home.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was granted the hereditary rank of baitalabula haqan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was granted the hereditary rank of baitalabula haqan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，噶爾丹擾邊，命西安將軍尼雅翰等出防寧夏，以軍事諮良棟。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Galdan harassed the frontier; Ni Yahang, General of Xi'an, and others were ordered out to guard Ningxia, and military affairs were referred to Liangdong for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year Galdan raided the frontier. General of Xi'an Ni Yahang and others were sent to guard Ningxia, and Liangdong was consulted on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，以寧夏總兵馮德昌赴甘州，命良棟暫領鎮兵。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, as Ningxia Regional Commander Feng Dechang went to Ganzhou, Liangdong was ordered temporarily to command the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year, when Ningxia Regional Commander Feng Dechang went to Ganzhou, Liangdong was ordered temporarily to command the Ningxia garrison.

sentences.zh: 良棟劾德昌剋軍糧，德昌坐罷。

translations.literal: Liangdong impeached Dechang for embezzling army grain, and Dechang was dismissed on conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong accused Feng Dechang of skimming army rations, and Feng was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，命良棟率兵駐土喇禦噶爾丹，旋召詣京師。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year Liangdong was ordered to lead troops to encamp at Tula to guard against Galdan, and soon afterward was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was ordered to take troops to Tula to guard against Galdan, then was soon recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，良棟復自陳戰功為大將軍圖海、彰泰所抑，並咎大學士明珠蔽功，上責其褊隘，還其疏，仍敕部優敘，授一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year Liangdong again set forth his battle achievements, saying they had been suppressed by Grand Generals Tu Hai and Zhang Zhangtai and also blaming Grand Secretary Mingzhu for concealing his merit; the Emperor rebuked his narrow-mindedness, returned his memorial, still ordered the ministry to grant him preferential reward, and appointed him a first-class jingqi nihaqan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year Liangdong again pleaded his battle record, claiming that Grand Generals Tu Hai and Zhang Zhangtai had suppressed it and that Grand Secretary Mingzhu had hidden his merits. The Emperor rebuked his pettiness, returned the memorial, but still ordered the ministry to reward him and granted him a first-class jingqi nihaqan.

sentences.zh: 良棟原留京師，乞田宅。

translations.literal: Liangdong had originally remained in the capital and asked for fields and a residence.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong had been staying in the capital and asked for land and a house.

sentences.zh: 御史龔翔麟劾良棟驕縱，上原之，賚白金二千，令歸里。

translations.literal: Censor Gong Xianglin impeached Liangdong for arrogance and license; the Emperor pardoned him, bestowed two thousand taels of white silver, and ordered him to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gong Xianglin accused him of arrogance and insubordination. The Emperor forgave him, gave him two thousand taels of silver, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，良棟病，尚書馬齊自寧夏還，奏狀，手詔存問，賜人葠、鹿尾。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year Liangdong fell ill; Minister Ma Qi returned from Ningxia and reported his condition; an autograph edict inquired after his health and granted ginseng and deer tail.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year Liangdong fell ill. Minister Ma Qi returned from Ningxia with a report on his condition. The Emperor sent a personal edict of inquiry and gifts of ginseng and deer tail.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年七十有七。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 上方徵噶爾丹，次榆林，諭曰：「良棟偉男子，著有功績。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then on campaign against Galdan and halted at Yulin; he instructed, saying: "Liangdong was a great man and achieved distinguished merit."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then campaigning against Galdan and halted at Yulin. He said: "Liangdong was a formidable man who won great distinction."

sentences.zh: 性躁心窄，每與人不合，奏事朕前，言語粗率。

translations.literal: "His nature was hot-tempered and his mind narrow; he constantly failed to get on with others, and when memorializing before Us his speech was rough and blunt."
translations.idiomatic: "He was quick-tempered and narrow-minded, often at odds with others, and when he spoke to me his words were blunt and rough."

sentences.zh: 朕保全功臣，始終優容之，所請無不允。

translations.literal: "We preserved this meritorious minister and showed him favor to the end; whatever he asked was never refused."
translations.idiomatic: "I meant to preserve a deserving servant and indulged him to the end. Nothing he asked was refused."

sentences.zh: 今病卒，宜為其妻子區處，使得安生。

translations.literal: "Now that he has died of illness, his wife and children ought to be provided for so that they may live in security."
translations.idiomatic: "Now that he has died of illness, see that his wife and children are provided for so they may live in peace."

sentences.zh: 」至寧夏，命皇長子允禔臨其喪，賜祭葬，諡襄忠。

translations.literal: When he reached Ningxia he ordered the eldest imperial son Yunzhi to attend the funeral in person, granted sacrificial rites and burial honors, and gave the posthumous name Xiangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At Ningxia he ordered the eldest imperial son Yunzhi to attend the funeral in person, granted state funeral honors, and gave him the posthumous name Xiangzhong.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，上諭群臣，猶舉良棟至雲南與彰泰議軍事，謂決於進戰乃得成切。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year the Emperor instructed the assembled ministers, still citing the recommendation to send Liangdong to Yunnan to deliberate military affairs with Zhang Zhangtai, and declared that only by resolving to advance and give battle could success be truly achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year the Emperor told his ministers that he had still recommended sending Liangdong to Yunnan to consult with Zhang Zhangtai on military affairs, and that true success depended on resolving to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十七年，進一等伯，世襲罔替。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Qianlong he was advanced to a first-class earl with perpetual hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year of Qianlong he was promoted to first-class earl with perpetual hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 子弘燦，初以廕生特授寧夏總兵，歷川北、真定、黃岩、南贛諸鎮。

translations.literal: His son Hongcan, at first specially appointed from yinsheng status as regional commander of Ningxia, served in succession at the garrisons of Chuanbei, Zhending, Huangyan, and Nan'gan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongcan was first specially appointed from yinsheng status as regional commander of Ningxia, then served at the garrisons of Chuanbei, Zhending, Huangyan, and Nan'gan in turn.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年，授浙江提督，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi he was appointed Provincial Military Commissioner of Zhejiang and transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi he was appointed provincial military commissioner of Zhejiang, then transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，授兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was appointed Governor-General of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was appointed governor-general of Liangguang.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，入覲，辭還，奏言久處炎海，年事就衰，請移近地自效。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he came to audience; on taking leave to return he memorialized that having long dwelt in the torrid sea he was declining in years and asked to be moved to a nearer region to serve.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year he came to court and, on taking leave to return home, memorialized that long service in the sultry south had worn on him with age and asked to be posted nearer home where he could still be of use.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，詣京師，至武昌，道卒，諡敏恪。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he proceeded to the capital; at Wuchang he died on the road, and his posthumous name was Minke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he set out for the capital but died on the road at Wuchang. His posthumous name was Minke.

sentences.zh: 弘燮，初授完縣知縣，再遷天津道。

translations.literal: Hongxie was first appointed magistrate of Wan County, then promoted to Intendant of Tianjin Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxie was first appointed magistrate of Wan County, then promoted to intendant of Tianjin Circuit.

sentences.zh: 良棟卒，襲一等精奇尼哈番，复授天津道。

translations.literal: When Liangdong died, he inherited the first-class jingqi nihaqan and was again appointed Intendant of Tianjin Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangdong died, Hongxie inherited the first-class jingqi nihaqan and was again appointed intendant of Tianjin Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三遷河南巡撫，調直隸。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Governor of Henan and was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became governor of Henan, then was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，諭獎弘燮撫直隸十年，任事勤勞，旗、民輯睦，盜案稀少，加總督銜。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year an edict praised Hongxie for ten years governing Zhili—diligent in office, Banner and commoner populations harmonious, and robbery cases few—and added the rank of governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year an edict praised Hongxie for ten years governing Zhili: diligent in duty, Banner and commoner populations well harmonized, and few robbery cases. He was given the rank of governor-general.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，卒，諡肅敏。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he died; his posthumous name was Sumin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he died. His posthumous name was Sumin.

sentences.zh: 弘燮在官虧庫帑，特命弘燦子之垣以郎中署直隸巡撫，責完補。

translations.literal: Hongxie while in office had a deficit in treasury funds; by special order Zhiyuan, son of Hongcan, was appointed acting Governor of Zhili in the capacity of director of a bureau, with responsibility to make good the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxie had run up a treasury deficit while in office. By special order Zhiyuan, Hongcan's son, was appointed acting governor of Zhili as a bureau director and charged with making up the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，以之垣庸劣，令解任。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor took the throne, deeming Zhiyuan mediocre and incompetent, he ordered him removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor took the throne, he found Zhiyuan mediocre and ordered him removed.

sentences.zh: 尋命免追虧項，詔謂念良棟舊勳也。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he ordered that recovery of the deficit be waived; the edict stated that this was in consideration of Liangdong's old merit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he ordered that recovery of the deficit be waived, the edict citing remembrance of Liangdong's former service.

sentences.zh: 王進寶，字顯吾，甘肅靖遠人。

translations.literal: Wang Jinbao, courtesy name Xianwu, was a native of Jingyuan in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinbao, courtesy name Xianwu, was a native of Jingyuan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 精騎射。

translations.literal: He excelled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從孟喬芳討定河西回，授守備，隸甘肅總兵張勇標下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shunzhi reign he followed Meng Qiaoang in the campaign to pacify the Hui of Hexi, was appointed garrison commander, and served under Gansu Regional Commander Zhang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign he followed Meng Qiaoang in pacifying the Muslims of Hexi, was appointed garrison commander, and served under Gansu regional commander Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，勇調經略右標總兵，南征，進寶從徇湖南。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Yong was transferred to be regional commander of the Grand Council's Right Banner; on the southern expedition Jinbao followed and campaigned in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Zhang Yong was transferred to regional commander of the Grand Council's Right Banner. On the southern expedition Jinbao followed and campaigned in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十五年，下貴州，師次十萬谿，懸崖千仞，明將李定國遣其將羅大順扼險屯守。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Guizhou was taken; the army halted at Shiwanxi, where cliffs rose a thousand ren. Ming general Li Dingguo sent his officer Luo Dashun to hold the pass and encamp.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Guizhou fell. The army halted at Shiwanxi, where cliffs rose a thousand ren high. Ming general Li Dingguo sent his officer Luo Dashun to hold the defile and encamp.

sentences.zh: 進寶率眾攀崖直上，搗其巢，大順奔潰，以功遷經略右標中營游擊。

translations.literal: Jinbao led his men straight up the cliff, stormed their nest, and Dashun fled in rout; for his merit he was transferred to brigade commander of the Right Banner Grand Council's Center Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Jinbao led his men straight up the cliff and stormed their stronghold. Dashun fled in rout. For this feat he was promoted to brigade commander of the Grand Council Right Banner's center brigade.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，勇還為甘肅提督，進寶亦改授提標左營游擊，隨軍有功，遷參將。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi Yong returned as Gansu Provincial Military Commissioner; Jinbao was also reassigned as brigade commander of the Provincial Brigade's Left Camp, followed the army with merit, and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi Zhang Yong returned as Gansu provincial military commissioner. Jinbao was reassigned brigade commander of the provincial brigade's left camp, served with merit on campaign, and was promoted to deputy commander.
